subject: EdgeBank - request for signed erase manifest and keystore rotation evidence
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgebank.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeBank Security Team <security@edgebank.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: extended signed erase manifest for tenant logs

Hi Rafael,

We’re finalizing a controls mapping for a regulatory review and need a narrow exception to the standard 30-day ephemeral debug-log retention for a single EdgeBank tenant (acct: EB-8942). The ask is not to change platform-wide defaults — only to capture and retain for 180 days a subset of tenant debug traces that are tagged with transaction correlation IDs for forensic review.

Specifically we require: 
- A signed "erase manifest" when those traces are deleted (manifest should include file paths, S3 object keys, deletion timestamp, and SHA256 digests)
- Evidence of KMS key rotation ids that apply to the objects while retained
- A short attestation describing how deletion predicates were scoped (so we can link to our auditors)

Can Redwood produce the manifest format and a sample proof-of-delete we can show to auditors? Also flag any SOC 2/SIG/CAIQ questions your security team thinks we should expect.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Director, Security Compliance
EdgeBank

(attachment: edgebank_sig_questionnaire_v2.xlsx)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended signed erase manifest for tenant logs

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask. We can support a customer-scoped retention carveout for forensic traces and produce a signed erase manifest on deletion. A few clarifying points and what we can deliver by default: 

1) Scope and technical controls
- We will only persist objects that are explicitly labeled by your integration with a tenant-scoped tag (metadata: tenant=EB-8942 AND retention_profile=forensic-180).
- Stored objects remain encrypted at rest with customer tenant keys (KMS). We can export KMS key rotation ids (rotation_event_id and timestamp) tied to the objects' lifecycle.

2) Signed erase manifest contents (we’ll provide a sample):
- object_key (S3 path), object_size_bytes, recorded_sha256, deletion_timestamp_utc, deleter_service (redwood-inference/runtime), manifest_signature (RSA-PSS base64)
- optional: snapshot_of_acl_and_metadata.json (when requested)

3) Proof-of-delete options for auditors
- Signed erase manifest (as above) — recommended primary artifact
- Optional: time-limited pre-deletion snapshot (read-only export) stored in our secure evidence bucket; we can produce a signed digest of that snapshot and then include the snapshot id in the manifest
- We can provide a high-level attestation template referencing SOC 2 controls and SIG/CAIQ mappings (we’ll coordinate with Security).

4) Operational SLA and retention mechanics
- Redwood will apply an escrow-like lifecycle policy for the bucket holding the forensic traces: retention enforced by service-level predicate; deletion executed by a scheduled job; manifest produced as part of the job run.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly (security) to confirm compliance artifacts and attestation language.
- We’ll prepare a sample erase-manifest and a short doc describing the delete predicate and storage ACLs.

Kimberly/Priya — can you weigh in on SOC 2 / SIG expectations and whether signed manifests are sufficient or if EdgeBank will want a signed time-stamped ledger entry (e.g., hash chain)?

Best,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgebank.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended signed erase manifest for tenant logs

Thanks Rafael / Alyssa — quick security input: 

- From a SOC 2 perspective (CC6/CC7), a signed erase manifest plus an internal audit trail that links the manifest to the deletion job is typically acceptable. Auditors often want: evidence that deletion was triggered, the job/actor who performed the deletion, and that the data was inaccessible after deletion. The manifest + job logs + keystore-rotation entries covers this triangle.

- For SIG/CAIQ reviewers: they will ask to map the artifacts to specific questions (e.g., SIG question DSI-1/DSI-2 around data disposal). We can produce a short mapping doc that references the exact manifest fields against SIG controls.

- Hash-chain vs single manifest signature: single signed manifest is usually sufficient. If EdgeBank prefers an append-only ledger, we can produce a time-stamped hash chain (we have an internal service that emits attestations to an append-only store; that is heavier operationally and may require a short SOC 2 change control).

Priya — operationally, the sample we provide should include: manifest json, job-run log (truncated), and keystore rotation CSV. Priya, can you draft the sample artifacts by EOD tomorrow?

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Security, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgebank.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Tom Wilkes <tom.wilkes@edgebank.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended signed erase manifest for tenant logs

Hi all — that sounds good. A few clarifications from our auditors: 
- The manifest must include SHA256 digests and an attestation that the objects were inaccessible post-delete (S3 object deletion alone is not enough; auditors like to see lifecycle enforcement plus evidence that the object is not recoverable via backups).
- Keystore evidence needs to show key rotation events during the 180-day window (rotation id, prior_key_id -> new_key_id, timestamp).
- We do not require a hash-chain for this engagement; signed manifests + job logs are adequate.

If you can provide the sample artifacts and the SIG mapping file, we’ll start our internal review. Ideally we’d get the sample before the end of the week.

Thanks,
Alyssa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@edgebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended signed erase manifest for tenant logs

Alyssa / Team — attaching the initial artifacts for review.

Attachments included: sample-erase-manifest-20270525.json (signed), keystore-rotation-log-202704.csv, and a one-page SIG mapping PDF (in the ZIP).

What’s in the sample manifest: 
- object_key: s3://redwood-evidence/EB-8942/forensic/trace-20270123-abc123.gz
- recorded_sha256: 9f2c4e... (truncated)
- deletion_timestamp_utc: 2027-05-25T08:00:00Z
- deletion_job_id: job-rt-7881
- manifest_signature: (RSA-PSS base64)

Operational notes: the deletion job also emits a job-run log (we included a truncated excerpt showing the job id, executor principal, and the pre-delete checksum verification). Keystore CSV lists rotation_event_id and mapping of key ids; we included the rotation that occurred during the retention window.

If this looks good, we’ll package the artifacts into a secure, time-limited evidence link and provide the signed manifest for your auditors.

Next: Rafael to send evidence link and proposed attestation text if EdgeBank accepts the sample.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
